parallel.requirements: Recognized the need to build an original fselect-compatible executable from black-box behavior and bundled docs only.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent kept implementation ownership while launching a large workflow of feature-area probe agents plus one extra date-lexer subagent.
parallel.implementation: The parent began a Go implementation and wrote only a module file and field metadata source before the run closed.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: No integrated executable source, build script, or completed CLI was assembled; the submitted tree had only partial Go sources alongside the original task files.
parallel.verification: The run performed many behavior probes, but the workflow did not return a complete report and no final integrated build verification occurred.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The workflow was killed with no result and the final artifact could not compile, leaving all official tests not run.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same black-box fselect reimplementation requirement and worked from documentation plus observed CLI behavior.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single agent performed research, probing, and implementation locally with workflow and agent delegation explicitly disabled.
serial.implementation: The serial attempt created a Rust project and wrote `rx.rs` and `digest.rs`, but did not finish the executable main program.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The submitted serial artifact contained `Cargo.toml` and two Rust modules but no `src/main.rs`, so it was not a buildable binary package.
serial.verification: The serial run carried out focused black-box probes but did not complete a build or official-aligned end-to-end acceptance check before timeout.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial attempt also timed out and failed compilation because the executable source was incomplete.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel understood the clean-room fselect reimplementation requirement and the prohibition on source lookup or wrapping.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial received and followed the same prompt, using the binary and bundled documentation as the behavior source.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition difference is visible; the later divergence is in allocation and implementation completion.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed behavior discovery into ten feature-area workflow probes plus a separate spawned probe while the parent began implementation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had workflows, tasks, and agents denied and therefore kept all research and coding in one agent.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent shared budget across many concurrent investigators; serial spent the budget on one continuous local investigation and implementation path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children received area-specific probe briefs and were told to return dense reports and write findings under `/tmp/findings`.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial needed no inter-agent handoff interface; its observations and implementation state stayed in one trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel plan depended on receiving many probe reports back through the workflow, whereas the serial path had no cross-agent reporting boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel started a Go implementation by creating `src/go.mod` and writing `src/field.go`.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial started a Rust implementation by creating a Cargo package and writing `rx.rs` and `digest.rs`.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both produced partial implementations, but in different languages and at different layers; neither reached a complete executable entry point.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The workflow did not complete or return aggregate results; the state record has `result:null` and `status:killed`.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child-result lifecycle to join, retrieve, or merge.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a failed multi-agent result lifecycle; serial's failure came from unfinished local coding rather than unreturned child work.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The final parallel artifact listed only `src/field.go` and `src/go.mod` as new source under `src`.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The final serial artifact listed `Cargo.toml`, `src/rx.rs`, and `src/digest.rs`, with no `src/main.rs`.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel delivered an incomplete Go skeleton; serial delivered incomplete Rust support modules. Both were unbuildable, but for different implementation contents.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The official evaluator completed and reported `compile_failed`, with all 3435 tests not run.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The official evaluator also completed and reported `compile_failed`, with all 3435 tests not run.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No official outcome difference exists; both attempts failed before behavioral tests could execute.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran for essentially the full 2399-second agent timeout while carrying an eleven-agent workflow footprint.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also timed out around 2399 seconds, but without workflow or subagent budget spent.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's closure pressure was tied to a broad live fan-out plus partial parent implementation; serial's closure pressure was a single-agent unfinished implementation.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations are not discordant: both parallel and serial failed compilation with zero of 3435 tests passing. The concrete process difference is that parallel lost budget to a killed broad probe workflow before a buildable Go executable existed, while serial stayed single-agent and still failed because the Rust executable source was incomplete.
parallel_contributors: Broad workflow fan-out returned no aggregate result before the run closed.
Submitted parallel artifact contained only `src/go.mod` and `src/field.go` under source.
serial_contributors: Serial kept all work local with delegation disabled.
Submitted serial artifact contained support modules but no `src/main.rs` executable entry point.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel chose a Go skeleton centered on field metadata, while serial chose a Rust project and spent effort on regex and digest modules.
Both failures were compile failures rather than observed semantic mismatches.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is a parallel-side adverse process contrast, not an explanation for a discordant score

candidates.reason: The parent kept implementation ownership and wrote source files; the implementation was incomplete rather than unassigned.
The delegated work was behavioral probing, not separately owned components requiring an integration owner.
The missing executable was a consequence of unfinished parent implementation under timeout, not an explicitly unowned assembly step.
The parent controlled research, implementation, and final delivery; there was no separate end-to-end pipeline ownership gap.
No single mandatory preflight gate blocked implementation; the parent began probing and Go source work while children ran.
Investigation was broad and concurrent, not a completed serial research phase followed by deadline-constrained implementation.
The observed allocation problem is more specifically collective fan-out budget exhaustion, not a generic underallocation of the critical path.

The parent launched ten exhaustive probe areas in parallel, the workflow state shows eleven child agents with `status:killed` and no result, and the run exhausted its finite budget before a buildable artifact existed.
candidates.realized_consequence: The broad probe workflow consumed the finite run window without returning aggregate findings, and the final parallel artifact contained only a partial Go skeleton that could not compile.
candidates.near_match_reason: The workflow was killed, but the directly corrective boundary is reducing the collective fan-out breadth; treating the same timeout chain as termination would duplicate the episode.

The child briefs stated the binary, docs, black-box rules, report format, and feature scopes; no already-known omitted requirement caused unusable child work.
The agents were assigned probe reports rather than interoperating components, so no missing component contract produced an incompatibility.
No completed child finding is shown being transferred and then lost before parent use.
The workflow produced no aggregate handoff at all, so there is no received bulk report that the parent failed to reduce.
There is no evidence the parent consumed a report describing superseded workspace or requirement state.
No incompatible returned reports or contracts reached the parent and remained unadjudicated at a decision point.
The parent did not make an observable whole-task completion decision; the run timed out with an empty final response and partial artifact.
There was no replacement or retry child repeating work without inherited findings or current workspace state.
